clinical_observations.content: Sabrina participated in an in-clinic evaluation with her mother present. Sabrina presented with a cheerful and cooperative affect but exhibited fluctuating attention spans which necessitated intermittent redirection. Muscle tone was within normal limits, and she displayed a full range of motion. Distractibility appeared to significantly affect her task engagement and task transitions required maximal verbal cues. She demonstrated greater participation during self-directed activities but needed substantial visual cues to sustain involvement in structured tasks. Fine motor coordination revealed some deficiencies, with visual-motor integration requiring hand-over-hand assistance, impacting the fluidity and accuracy of her movements. Behavioral observations included signs of frustration during challenging tasks, necessitating additional support to ensure the validity of standardized test results. Testing modifications included extended breaks and encouragement to bolster task completion.
